title: Copper Notches 11th Weekly Gain in Twelve on Chinese Buying

title: Earnings, Not the Fed, Are Driving Stocks: UBS's Lovell
summary: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says strong earnings and broadening profit growth should keep stocks moving higher even as rising rates create near-term volatility. “What’s gonna drive this market is earnings. It’s not valuation expansion,” Lovell says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: How Beer Distributors and Other “Little Guys” Got Rich
summary:
America's “Main Street Millionaires” comprise about three million private business owners who have amassed one of the country's most concentrated pools of wealth. That's according to a study conducted by Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick.

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, economists and authors of The Everywhere Millionaire: Who Is Really Rich in America and How They Got There, tell Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal how "little guys" like beverage distributors, dentists and car wash owners have become millionaires hiding in plain sight. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Pares BOJ-Fueled Declines as Nikkei Reports a Rate Check
summary: The yen pared declines on Friday, with the Nikkei newspaper reporting that the Bank of Japan inquired with market participants about exchange-rate levels, a step often seen as a precursor to official intervention.

title: Investor Sentiment Plunges to 16-Month Low, AAII Survey Shows
summary: Investor sentiment fell to its lowest point since 2025, a weekly survey from the American Association of Individual Investors showed, as oil prices remained elevated while the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.

title: VW Slashes Outlook After China Sales Slump, Costs Weigh
summary: Volkswagen AG slashed its profit forecast after a sharp contraction in China and a €6 billion ($6.9 billion) writedown tied to sports-car maker Porsche AG, deepening concerns about the strains facing the global auto industry.

title: College Students Look for Leg Up to Get Wall Street Job
summary: Bloomberg Finance Editor Daniel Taub talks about the lengths college students are going to as they try to land a lucrative job on Wall Street. He speaks on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'Hike Doesn't Change Fundamentals,' says Cetera's Goldman
summary:
Gene Goldman, CIO of Cetera, reacts to the inflation expectations and overall market volatility following the Fed's rate decision by telling Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu that it's one and done (maybe two and done), not the start of something bigger. It's insurance against sticky inflation, not a return to aggressive tightening.
Markets had priced in too much. 
Federal Reserve officials failed to adequately respond to repeated warnings about the deteriorating financial condition of Silicon Valley Bank before its 2023 failure, a new draft report found, according to Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and other people familiar with the document. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Saudis Give European Oil Buyers No Supplies for Next Month
summary: Saudi Aramco told at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will be allocated no crude next month under long-term agreements after the kingdom’s key pipeline to the Red Sea was attacked, people informed of the decision said.

title: Big Take: If You Work, Are You ‘Working Class’?
summary: The definition of "working class" in the US has been shifting over the last couple of decades with changes in the economic and labor market, and advances in AI are going to change the traditional white collar market, too. With midterms right around the corner, who are candidates talking about talking about when they campaign for the working class vote? (Source: Bloomberg)
